intro: An IEC 61850 device has no register numbers. It has a tree of named objects, described in its SCL file: logical devices, logical nodes, data objects and attributes. A client walks that tree with MMS and reads, or writes, exactly the value it needs.

connect.title: Connect
connect.text: The client opens TCP to port 102, then an ISO transport connection on top of it (COTP).

associate.title: Associate
associate.text: An MMS Initiate agrees on sizes and services. Only after this association can the client ask questions.

browse.title: Browse the model
browse.text: GetNameList returns the logical devices, then the variables inside one. This is how a tool discovers a device without its SCL file.

read.title: Read one value
read.text: The client reads PV1INV/MMXU1$MX$TotW$mag$f and gets a float: 4820.0. The unit, kW, is a separate attribute (CF).

report.title: Let it report
report.text: Instead of asking again and again, the client enables a report. The inverter now sends its values when they change.

frames.initiate-req: Let's talk MMS: my sizes and services
frames.names-req: Which logical devices do you have?
frames.read-req: What is the total active power?

notes.tcp: Plain TCP. MMS uses port 102, the ISO-on-TCP port of RFC 1006.
notes.cotp-cr: COTP (ISO 8073) runs on top of TCP. Its connect request names the transport selectors of both sides.
notes.cotp-cc: The device accepts. From now on, every message starts with TPKT and a COTP data header.
notes.initiate-req: Inside it are three more layers: session, presentation and ACSE. The MMS part offers sizes (the largest message) and the services the client wants.
notes.initiate-resp: The device answers with its own sizes and services. Authentication, when used, happens in this step too (IEC 62351-4).
notes.names-req: GetNameList with the object class "domain": in IEC 61850 a domain is a logical device.
notes.names-resp: MMS names a logical device by the IED name followed by its instance: PV1 and INV make PV1INV.
notes.enable: A Write of TRUE to RptEna in the report control block. The client sets the trigger options and the data set first.
notes.report: An unsolicited InformationReport: the device sends it without being asked, each time a value in the data set changes.

tpkt-66.name: TPKT
tpkt-66.note: Version 3, then the length of the whole message: 0x0042 = 66 bytes.

cotp-dt.name: COTP
cotp-dt.note: A data unit (0xF0), the last of its message (0x80).

session.name: Session
session.note: Two short session headers: give tokens, data transfer.

presentation.name: Presentation
presentation.note: Fully encoded data, presentation context 3: what follows is MMS.

confirmed-req.name: Confirmed request
confirmed-req.note: Tag A0, 44 bytes: a request that expects an answer.

invoke.name: Invoke ID 5
invoke.note: A number the client picks. The answer carries the same one.

invoke-resp.name: Invoke ID 5
invoke-resp.note: The same number as the request: this answers it.

spec.name: Variable list
spec.note: A list of one variable, given by its name.

domain-specific.name: Domain-specific name
domain-specific.note: A name in two parts: the domain and the item.

item.name: Item
item.note: "MMXU1$MX$TotW$mag$f": logical node, functional constraint, data object and attribute, joined by $.

results.name: Results
results.note: A list of results, one per variable asked for.

exponent.name: Exponent width
exponent.note: 8 bits: an IEEE 754 single-precision float follows.

float.name: Value
float.note: 4820.0, most significant byte first. IEC 104 sends floats the other way round.

a-ld.name: Logical device
a-ld.note: PV1INV: IED name PV1 and instance INV.

a-fc.name: Functional constraint
a-fc.note: MX: measured values. ST is status, CF configuration, SP set points.

a-do.name: Data object
a-do.note: TotW: total active power, of type MV.

a-da.name: Data attribute
a-da.note: mag.f: the magnitude, as a float.

facts.model: IEC 61850-7: logical devices, logical nodes, data objects

tips: Read the SCL file first. Browsing a large device with GetNameList can take many seconds.
Units and multipliers live in CF attributes, not next to the value. A value of 4820 is in kW only because the device says so.
Report control blocks are few. A tool that reserves one and never frees it can lock out the real SCADA.
MMS floats are sent most significant byte first. Code that also speaks IEC 104 or Modbus often gets this wrong.

anatomy.reference: The name of one value, and how MMS writes it

playground.scl: The inverter's configured description (.cid). Open INV, then MMXU1, then TotW: the value you read is mag.f, its unit is in units. Then open your own file, if you have one.
playground.encoder: MMS sends a float most significant byte first (ABCD). Type a value to see its bytes.
